As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support, starting from the general availability date of Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat. In line with this policy, support for Adobe Acrobat 10.x and Adobe Reader 10.x ended on November 15, 2015.

As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support, starting from the general availability date of Adobe Reader and Adobe Acrobat. In line with this policy, support for Adobe Acrobat 11.x and Adobe Reader 11.x ends on October 15, 2017.

As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support starting from the date of general availability date of Acrobat 2020. In line with this policy, support for Acrobat 2020 ends on November 30, 2025.

As stated in the Adobe Support Lifecycle Policy , Adobe provides five years of product support, starting from the general availability date of Adobe Acrobat and Acrobat Reader. In line with this policy, support for Adobe Acrobat 2017 Classic and Acrobat Reader 2017 Classic ends on June 06, 2022.

notes: Tier: researched (AGENTS.md rule 8b). endoflife.date has no acrobat product (checked https://endoflife.date/api/all.json 2026-09-17: no acrobat/acrobat-reader slug) and data/products/ holds no acrobat record; the existing data/products/coldfusion.json is a different Adobe product and is untouched. Scope: paid Acrobat desktop Pro/Standard lines only. Free Acrobat Reader is a separate product with its own contribution (contributions/adobe-acrobat-reader.json) and its Reader rows are deliberately absent here. The subscription Continuous (evergreen Document Cloud) track is excluded explicitly: it has no row on the vendor matrix at all (the matrix lists versioned lines only), so it carries no published lifecycle date and none is invented. Dates are the matrix's own cells: End of core support is the terminal supported date the vendor states, and where the cell carries an extension (2015, 2020: extended until 7/7/2020 and 11/30/2025) the extension is stored as the end-of-life date because it is the last date the product is supported, exactly as the matrix states it. End of extended support is N/A on every Acrobat row, so eos/eossec stay null. Every matrix Acrobat-named row is accounted for: 18 Pro/Standard/Pro Extended rows are published as 9 version cycles above; Acrobat & Review Comment Connector (1, 1.1) is a review connector, not a desktop Acrobat release; Acrobat 3D 8.x is an add-on that shipped with Acrobat 8; Acrobat Elements 7.x is an OEM/volume edition, not Pro or Standard; Acrobat Elements Server (6, 6.0.1) is a server product; Acrobat X Suite 10 is a bundle containing Acrobat X Pro and is not itself a Pro/Standard release (its 10 cycle dates are already published from the X Pro/X Standard rows). Every matrix date is mm/dd/yyyy (the page's own note: All dates in mm/dd/yyyy format); this contribution therefore also needs the contribute.py day matcher to read US M/D/YYYY spellings - requested from the engine owner with exact examples, see the handoff note. A date is never inferred: 2024's core support date is quoted as stated, and no other 2024 line is asserted. Adobe's own notice for Acrobat 2015 (/acrobat/kb/end-of-support-acrobat-2015-reader-2015.html, the link the matrix itself carries) now redirects to the Acrobat desktop hub and no longer states that date, so 2015 is cited to the matrix only; the X, XI, 2017 Classic and 2020 notice sentences above are quoted verbatim from the live notices Adobe still serves. Acrobat X Suite 10 and Acrobat Elements rows are excluded as bundles/OEM editions, and the Continuous (evergreen) track is excluded because the matrix carries no row for it.
